title: The trumpet-player MP who had to insult Lester for show
summary: Jones describes a white trumpet player-turned-MP who had to insult Lester before black prisoners to keep up appearances.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Do you remember what this trumpet player's name was?
It's in a book. I would like to not because -
But this trumpet player with tears in his eyes had to call Lester a nigger and Lester had to say, 'Yessir boss,' because in front of the black prisoners of war he had -
Was this a white trumpet player?
Well how can you possibly say he had to call him a nigger?
He's got to look good in front of the black people, but didn't nobody know what was happening but he and Lester. Do you understand? It was a subterfuge.
You had to do that. That's what I mean; it's very difficult for you to conceive this.
see he had to say something...
Not that he had to call him a nigger... I can
No, no, no, he had to call him a flat hook, to make it look good. If he had, "Come on, Lester," the other black people would say, "Who is he?" They put him in a sweat box.
What about the word soldier, which you were?
That didn't figure, Milt. You would have to be there.

Yeh, you would have to be there. It's authentic and he had to go through that, say, "Yessir boss," and then after everybody was gone Lester and I with about 15 musicians playing in the Rec' Hall all day long - ding,ding-a ding-ding-a-ding - and then when it was time to put him on the other side of the tracks he had to say, "Yessir boss." But Lester couldn't tell the black people what he was going through, because if Lester had a did that he'd have been dead. They'd a killed him. Do you understand?
